overviews.headline: FEMA Aid Deadline Nears for Tennessee Storm Survivors
overviews.summary: Tennesseans affected by the April 2-24 severe storms, tornadoes and flooding have until Aug. 19 to apply for FEMA assistance, with Disaster Recovery Centers adjusting their hours to help with applications.

timeline.text: Disaster Recovery Center hours change starting July 21, with centers open weekdays and Saturday mornings ahead of the Aug. 19 deadline.
FEMA announces one month remains for Tennessee storm survivors to apply for assistance, with an Aug. 19 deadline.

episode_cards.headline: One Month Left to Apply for FEMA Assistance After Tennessee April Severe Storms
episode_cards.summary: One Month Left to Apply for FEMA Assistance After Tennessee April Severe Storms Middle and Western Tennesseans who have been affected by April severe storms, straight-line winds, tornadoes and flooding have one month left to apply for FEMA assistance.Homeowners, renters, students, self-employed, ranchers and farmers in Cheatham, Davidson, Dickson, Dyer, Hardeman, McNairy, Montgomery, Obion and Wilson counties who were displaced or have property damage from the April 2-24 storms have until Tuesday, Aug. 19 to submit an application for FEMA assistance.Money is available for survivors who need help covering uninsured costs for things like rental expenses, home repairs, vehicle damage, medical expenses, moving and storage, and reimbursement for temporary housing.How to Apply for FEMA AssistanceApply online at DisasterAssistance.gov, use the FEMA App for mobile devices or call the FEMA Helpline at 800-621-3362. In-person help is available at any Disaster Recovery Center for submitting applications, getting updates and asking questions. episode_cards.headline: Hours to Change at Disaster Recovery Centers in Tennessee
episode_cards.summary: Hours to Change at Disaster Recovery Centers in Tennessee Middle and Western Tennesseans who experienced damage from the April 2-24 severe storms can get in-person assistance at FEMA Disaster Recovery Centers. The deadline to apply for assistance is Aug. 19.Money is available for survivors who need help covering uninsured costs for things like rental expenses, home repairs, vehicle damage, medical expenses, moving and storage, and reimbursement for temporary housing. overviews.headline: VA's Nursing Home to Home program helps Veterans return to community living
overviews.summary: The VA's Nursing Home to Home program has helped 61 Veterans, including 92-year-old Henry White, transition from nursing homes back into their own homes or community-based settings.

timeline.text: VA reports 61 Veterans returned home or to community settings through Nursing Home to Home program.
92-year-old Veteran Henry White leaves long-term care to age at home through the program.

episode_cards.headline: Nursing Home to Home program reunites Veteran and family
episode_cards.summary: Nursing Home to Home gives 92-year-old Henry White the chance to leave long-term care and age at home.

episode_cards.headline: From nursing homes to homes
episode_cards.summary: The Nursing Home to Home program has successfully facilitated the return of 61 Veterans to their own home or a community-based setting.

overviews.headline: USGS Monitors Ongoing Kīlauea Summit Eruption with UAS Survey and Episode 29 Fountaining
overviews.summary: USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory conducted a drone survey of the Kīlauea summit eruption site on July 17, followed by Episode 29 of sustained lava fountaining at Halemaʻumaʻu, which ended after over 13 hours on July 20, 2025.

timeline.text: Episode 29 of the Halemaʻumaʻu eruption ended after over 13 hours of sustained lava fountaining.
USGS HVO staff flew a UAS mission over the recent eruption site at Kīlauea summit.

episode_cards.headline: Photo & Video Chronology — July 17, 2025 — UAS mission at Kīlauea summit
episode_cards.summary: On July 17, USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory staff conducted a UAS (uncrewed aircraft systems) flight of the recent eurption site at Kīlauea summit.

episode_cards.headline: Photo & Video Chronology — July 20, 2025 — Episode 29 at Kīlauea summit
episode_cards.summary: Episode 29 of the ongoing Halemaʻumaʻu eruption ended at 6:35 p.m. HST, July 20, 2025, after over 13 hours of sustained lava fountaining.

overviews.headline: USPS Celebrates 250th Anniversary with Stamps and Events
overviews.summary: The U.S. Postal Service is marking its 250th founding anniversary on July 26 with special events, merchandise, and the unveiling of two new commemorative stamps.

timeline.text: USPS unveils two new commemorative stamp designs celebrating its history and everyday presence.
USPS announces a week of events to celebrate its 250th anniversary, including merchandise, digital media, and a stamp contest.

episode_cards.headline: Celebrating 250 Years of Connecting Communities: The Postal Service Marks a Proud Anniversary
episode_cards.summary: WASHINGTON — The Postal Service will mark the 250th anniversary of its founding on July 26. To celebrate the organization’s rich history of connecting people, communities and businesses, USPS will hold a series of special events this week and highlight other activities, including licensed merchandise, digital media, a stamp contest and special signage at Post Offices.

episode_cards.headline: Signed, Sealed and Delivered for 250 Years
episode_cards.summary: WASHINGTON — In celebration of two and a half centuries of continuous service, the U.S. Postal Service today unveiled two stamp releases at its headquarters building. The two stamp designs capture the essence of USPS, one honoring its deep-rooted history, the other highlighting its ubiquitous presence in everyday life.

overviews.headline: US Cracks Down on Haitian Gang Ties Among Legal Residents
overviews.summary: The State Department announced deportation actions against U.S. lawful permanent residents linked to Haitian gang network Viv Ansanm, and USCIS helped ICE arrest a Haitian national accused of contributing to Haiti's destabilization.

timeline.text: USCIS assists ICE in arresting Pierre Reginald Boulus for contributing to Haiti's destabilization.
State Department announces deportation actions against U.S. legal permanent residents tied to Haitian gang leaders.

episode_cards.headline: USCIS Assists in Investigation Leading to Arrest of Haitian Engaged in Violence and Destabilization of Haiti
episode_cards.summary: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services provided valuable assistance in the investigation that led to Immigration and Customs Enforcement arresting Pierre Reginald Boulus on July 17 for violating the Immigration and Nationality Act by contributing to the destabilization of Haiti.
